name: Dark Taupe
lede: Dark Taupe is a deep, warm grey-brown, a shade down from [[taupe]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a grayish yellowish brown, one of the most common swatches in our archive.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark taupe" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is grayish yellowish brown, a little over 3 CIEDE2000 units away, with a Munsell reading near 9.8YR in hue [1]. Its nearest named neighbors in our library are [[taupe]], [[sepia]] and [[umber]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 5,350 of 23,781 paintings, or about 22 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is far more common in early paintings, running 3.4 times the archive's baseline rate in the 1270s and still over 3 times the baseline across the whole 1100s [2]. It is especially common in Korean, Japanese and Chinese works, and the word "Sepia" shares its canvases more than chance [2]. Across all the paintings that carry it, it splits fairly evenly between a mid-tone and a highlight [2].
